1: GNU Octave -- a high-level language for numerical computations
2: ==============================================================
3: 
4: Copyright (C) 1996-2026 The Octave Project Developers
5: 
6: See the file COPYRIGHT.md in the top-level directory of this

8: 
9: Overview
10: --------
11: 
12: GNU Octave is a high-level interpreted language, primarily intended
13: for numerical computations.  It provides capabilities for the
14: numerical solution of linear and nonlinear problems, and for
15: performing other numerical experiments.  It also provides extensive
16: graphics capabilities for data visualization and manipulation.  GNU
17: Octave is normally used through its interactive interface (CLI and
18: GUI), but it can also be used to write non-interactive programs.
19: The GNU Octave language is quite similar to Matlab so that most
20: programs are easily portable.
21: 
22: GNU Octave is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify it
23: under the terms of the GNU General Public License as published by
24: the Free Software Foundation, either version 3 of the License, or
25: (at your option) any later version.
26: 
27: GNU Octave is distributed in the hope that it will be useful, but
28: WITHOUT ANY WARRANTY; without even the implied warranty of
29: MERCHANTABILITY or FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.  See the
30: GNU General Public License for more details.
31: 
32: You should have received a copy of the GNU General Public License
33: along with Octave; see the file COPYING.  If not, see
34: <https://www.gnu.org/licenses/>.
35: 
36: Availability
37: ------------
38: 
39: The latest released version of Octave is always available from
40: <https://ftp.gnu.org/gnu/octave/> and many mirror sites around the
41: world.  You may also find links to binary distributions at
42: <https://www.octave.org/download.html>.  The current development
43: sources may be found under the Source Code tab on
44: [Savannah](https://savannah.gnu.org/projects/octave/).
45: 
46: You are encouraged to verify the Octave installation file you download
47: (such as `octave-11.1.0.tar.xz`) as follows:
48: * First, ensure that you are downloading from the official Octave website, or
49: from a GNU mirror linked from the official Octave website.
50: * Next, download the corresponding signature file for the installation file
51: you downloaded, for example `octave-11.1.0.tar.xz.sig`.
52: * Next, run the command
53: ```
54:   gpg --keyserver hkps://keys.gnupg.net --recv-keys B05F05B75D36644B
55: ```
56: to import John W. Eaton's public key (this needs to be done only once).
57: * Verify the integrity of the file you downloaded with a command like
58: ```
59:   gpg --verify octave-11.1.0.tar.xz.sig
60: ```
61: * If all is well, then the output should say
62: ```
63:   gpg: Good signature from "John W. Eaton <jwe@gnu.org>
64: ```
65: * If the file you downloaded was corrupted or changed by anyone else, then
66: the output will say
67: ```
68:   gpg: BAD signature from "John W. Eaton <jwe@gnu.org>"
69: ```
70: If so, you should not install Octave from that file, but should start over.
71: 
72: Installation
73: ------------
74: 
75: Building Octave from source requires approximately 475 MB of disk space (or
76: approximately 3.8 GB with debugging symbols).  Once installed, Octave uses
77: approximately 75 MB of disk space (or approximately 415 MB if shared libraries
78: are not built or binaries include debugging symbols).
79: 
80: To compile Octave, you will need a recent version of:

GNU Octave is a high-level interpreted language, primarily intended

graphics capabilities for data visualization and manipulation.  GNU

GUI), but it can also be used to write non-interactive programs.

Availability
------------

The latest released version of Octave is always available from
<https://ftp.gnu.org/gnu/octave/> and many mirror sites around the
world.  You may also find links to binary distributions at
<https://www.octave.org/download.html>.  The current development
sources may be found under the Source Code tab on
[Savannah](https://savannah.gnu.org/projects/octave/).

You are encouraged to verify the Octave installation file you download
(such as `octave-11.1.0.tar.xz`) as follows:
* First, ensure that you are downloading from the official Octave website, or
from a GNU mirror linked from the official Octave website.
* Next, download the corresponding signature file for the installation file
you downloaded, for example `octave-11.1.0.tar.xz.sig`.
* Next, run the command
```
  gpg --keyserver hkps://keys.gnupg.net --recv-keys B05F05B75D36644B
```
to import John W. Eaton's public key (this needs to be done only once).
* Verify the integrity of the file you downloaded with a command like
```
  gpg --verify octave-11.1.0.tar.xz.sig
```
* If all is well, then the output should say
```
  gpg: Good signature from "John W. Eaton <jwe@gnu.org>
```
* If the file you downloaded was corrupted or changed by anyone else, then
the output will say
```

```
If so, you should not install Octave from that file, but should start over.

------------

Building Octave from source requires approximately 475 MB of disk space (or
approximately 3.8 GB with debugging symbols).  Once installed, Octave uses
approximately 75 MB of disk space (or approximately 415 MB if shared libraries
are not built or binaries include debugging symbols).

308: ### Determine which C++ compiler to use (we expect to find g++ or clang++).
309: 
310: # AC_PROG_CXX attempts to find the compiler flags for activating support for
311: # C++11.  As of autoconf version 2.71, the source code that it uses for that
312: # test includes parts that are invalid in C++20.
313: # We are using AX_CXX_COMPILE_STDCXX to determine the potentially needed flags
314: # for the C++ version that Octave requires.  So, skip the (unnecessary and
315: # broken) test for C++11 in AC_PROG_CXX by setting the following (undocumented)
316: # flag:
317: ac_cv_prog_cxx_cxx11=""
318: AC_PROG_CXX
319: AC_PROG_CXXCPP
320: 
321: ## Ensure that the C++ compiler fully supports C++20.
322: ## Preferably with GNU extensions if flags are required.
323: AX_CXX_COMPILE_STDCXX(20, [], mandatory)
324: 
325: ENABLE_STD_PMR_POLYMORPHIC_ALLOCATOR=yes
326: AC_ARG_ENABLE(std-pmr-polymorphic-allocator,
327:   [AS_HELP_STRING([--disable-std-pmr-polymorphic-allocator],
328:                   [build libraries without support for std::pmr::polymorphic_allocator, less efficient transfer of arrays to external MEX files])],
329:   [case $enableval in
330:      yes) ENABLE_STD_PMR_POLYMORPHIC_ALLOCATOR=yes ;;
331:      no) ENABLE_STD_PMR_POLYMORPHIC_ALLOCATOR=no ;;
332:      *) AC_MSG_ERROR([bad value $enableval for --enable-std-pmr-polymorphic-allocator]) ;;
333:    esac])
334: 
335: AC_ARG_WITH([qt],
336:   [AS_HELP_STRING([--with-qt=VER], [use the Qt major version VER])
337: dnl Second help string must not be indented for correct alignment
338: AS_HELP_STRING([--without-qt], [don't use Qt libraries, disable Qt GUI])],
339:   [case $withval in
340:      yes | "")
341:      ;;
342:      no)
343:        QT_VERSIONS=
344:      ;;
345:      *)
346:        QT_VERSIONS="$withval"
347:      ;;
348:    esac])
349: 
350: ### Determine C++ compiler capabilities.
351: 
352: if test $ENABLE_STD_PMR_POLYMORPHIC_ALLOCATOR = yes; then
353:   OCTAVE_CHECK_STD_PMR_POLYMORPHIC_ALLOCATOR
354: else
355:   HAVE_STD_PMR_POLYMORPHIC_ALLOCATOR="no"
356: fi
357: 
358: ### Determine which C compiler to use (we expect to find gcc or clang).
359: 
360: AC_PROG_CC
361: AC_PROG_CPP
362: 
363: ## Save and restore CFLAGS and CXXFLAGS globally.
364: dnl These variables are for users, so we shouldn't be touching them.
365: dnl Instead, we should set the corresponding AM_ flags (currently by way of the
366: dnl XTRA_ variables).  However, for the duration of the configure script, we
367: dnl may set CFLAGS and CXXFLAGS so that subsequent tests succeed.  Temporary
368: dnl settings like this are currently done for pthreads and openmp, for example.
369: original_octave_configure_CFLAGS="$CFLAGS"
370: original_octave_configure_CXXFLAGS="$CXXFLAGS"
371: 
372: ## Check for MSVC
373: have_msvc=no
374: case $host_os in
375:   msdosmsvc)
376:     have_msvc=yes
377:   ;;
378:   mingw*)
379:     AC_MSG_CHECKING([for MSVC compiler])
380:     AC_PREPROC_IFELSE([AC_LANG_SOURCE([[
381:         #if ! defined (_MSC_VER)
382:         #error "Not MSVC compiler"
383:         #endif
384:         ]])],
385:       have_msvc=yes, have_msvc=no)
386:     AC_MSG_RESULT([$have_msvc])
387:   ;;
388: esac
389: 
390: ### gnulib initialization: part 1
391: dnl Must take place immediately after a compiler is determined
392: 
393: gl_EARLY
394: 
395: ### Record version number when using g++.
396: 
397: GXX_VERSION=
398: if test "$GXX" = yes; then
399:   AC_CACHE_CHECK([g++ compiler version number],
400:     [octave_cv_gxx_version],
401:     [octave_cv_gxx_version=[`$CXX -v 2>&1 | $GREP "^.*g.. version" | $SED -e 's/^.*g.. version *//' -e 's/cygnus-//' -e 's/egcs-//' -e 's/ .*//'`]
402:   ])
403: 
404:   GXX_VERSION=$octave_cv_gxx_version
405: fi
406: AC_SUBST(GXX_VERSION)
407: 
408: ### Record version number when using gcc.
409: dnl It might be different from the g++ version number.
410: 
411: GCC_VERSION=
412: if test "$GCC" = yes; then
413:   AC_CACHE_CHECK([gcc compiler version number],
414:     [octave_cv_gcc_version],
415:     [octave_cv_gcc_version=[`$CC -v 2>&1 | $GREP "^.*gcc version" | $SED -e 's/^.*g.. version *//' -e 's/cygnus-//' -e 's/egcs-//' -e 's/ .*//'`]
416:   ])
417: 
418:   GCC_VERSION=$octave_cv_gcc_version
419: fi
420: AC_SUBST(GCC_VERSION)
421: 
422: ## It seems that there are some broken inline assembly functions in GNU libc.
423: ## Since it is uncertain how to test whether Octave is linked against GNU libc,
424: ## just disable them for all platforms.
425: 
426: AC_MSG_NOTICE([defining __NO_MATH_INLINES avoids buggy GNU libc exp function])
427: AC_DEFINE(__NO_MATH_INLINES, 1,
428:   [Define to 1 if your version of GNU libc has buggy inline assembly code for math functions like exp.])
429: 
430: ### Determine the compiler flag necessary to create dependencies.
431: 
432: ## Assume GCC.
433: INCLUDE_DEPS=yes
434: DEPEND_FLAGS="-M"
435: DEPEND_EXTRA_SED_PATTERN=""
436: if test "$GCC" != yes; then
437:   case $canonical_host_type in
438:     sparc-sun-solaris2* | i386-pc-solaris2*)
439:       DEPEND_FLAGS="-xM1"
440:       DEPEND_EXTRA_SED_PATTERN="-e '/\/opt\/SUNWspro/d'"
441:     ;;
442:     *-*-msdosmsvc)
443:     ;;
444:     *-*-mingw*)
445:       if test $have_msvc = no; then
446:         INCLUDE_DEPS=no
447:       fi
448:     ;;
449:     *)
450:       INCLUDE_DEPS=no
451:     ;;
452:   esac
453: fi
454: AC_SUBST(INCLUDE_DEPS)
455: AC_SUBST(DEPEND_FLAGS)
456: AC_SUBST(DEPEND_EXTRA_SED_PATTERN)
457: 
458: ### Check for math library.
459: dnl If found, this will add -lm to LIBS.
460: 
461: dnl Keep this check before the check for the Fortran compiler,
462: dnl in case -lm is needed to compile Fortran programs.
463: AC_CHECK_LIB(m, sin)
464: 
465: ### Determine the Fortran compiler and how to invoke it.
466: 
467: ## Prefer gfortran, but the user's F77 environment variable will override.
468: AC_PROG_F77([gfortran])
469: if test -z "$F77"; then
470:   ## No gfortran found, search for any other installed compiler.
471:   AC_PROG_F77
472: fi
473: if test "$F77" = g77; then
474:   AC_MSG_ERROR([g77 is not a supported Fortran compiler.  Select another compiler by setting the environment variable F77 and re-running configure.])
475: fi
476: 
477: AC_MSG_CHECKING([whether a usable Fortran compiler was found])
478: if test -n "$F77"; then
479:   AC_MSG_RESULT(yes)
480: else
481:   AC_MSG_RESULT(no)
482:   AC_MSG_ERROR([a Fortran compiler is required to build Octave])
483: fi
484: 
485: AC_F77_LIBRARY_LDFLAGS
486: AC_F77_DUMMY_MAIN
487: AC_F77_WRAPPERS
488: 
489: ## Must appear after checks for Fortran compiler.
490: OCTAVE_CHECK_FORTRAN_SYMBOL_AND_CALLING_CONVENTIONS
491: 
492: ## Must appear after checks for all compilers.
493: OCTAVE_DEFINE_MKOCTFILE_DYNAMIC_LINK_OPTIONS
494: 
495: ### Use a 64-bit integer type for array dimensions and indexing, if possible.
496: 
497: AC_CHECK_SIZEOF([int])
498: AC_DEFINE_UNQUOTED(OCTAVE_SIZEOF_INT, [$ac_cv_sizeof_int],
499:   [Define to the size of int.])
500: 
501: AC_CHECK_SIZEOF([void *])
502: if test $ac_cv_sizeof_void_p -ge 8; then
503:   ENABLE_64=yes
504: else
505:   ENABLE_64=no
506: fi
507: 
508: AC_ARG_ENABLE(64,
509:   [AS_HELP_STRING([--disable-64],
510:     [don't use 64-bit integers for array dimensions and indexing])],
511:   [case $enableval in
512:      yes) ENABLE_64=yes ;;
513:      no) ENABLE_64=no ;;
514:      *) AC_MSG_ERROR([bad value $enableval for --enable-64]) ;;
515:    esac])
516: 
517: if test $ENABLE_64 = yes; then
518:   if test $ac_cv_sizeof_void_p -ge 8; then
519:     OCTAVE_IDX_TYPE=int64_t
520:   else
521:     warn_64_bit="--enable-64 option given but pointers are less than 64-bits wide; disabling 64-bit indexing"
522:     OCTAVE_CONFIGURE_WARNING([warn_64_bit])
523:     OCTAVE_IDX_TYPE=int32_t
524:     ENABLE_64=no
525:   fi
526: else
527:   OCTAVE_IDX_TYPE=int32_t
528: fi
529: 
530: AC_SUBST(ENABLE_64)
531: if test $ENABLE_64 = yes; then
532:   octave_sizeof_octave_idx_type=8
533:   AC_DEFINE(OCTAVE_ENABLE_64, 1,
534:     [Define to 1 to use 64-bit integers for array dimensions and indexing.])
535: else
536:   octave_sizeof_octave_idx_type=4
537: fi
538: 
539: AC_DEFINE_UNQUOTED(OCTAVE_SIZEOF_IDX_TYPE, [$octave_sizeof_octave_idx_type],
540:   [Define to the size of the octave_idx_type (8 or 4).])
541: 
542: AC_SUBST(OCTAVE_IDX_TYPE)
543: AC_DEFINE_UNQUOTED(OCTAVE_IDX_TYPE, [$OCTAVE_IDX_TYPE],
544:   [Define to the type of octave_idx_type (64 or 32 bit signed integer).])
545: 
546: ### Check for LLVM or Apple libc++ library.
547: 
548: OCTAVE_LLVM_LIBCXX
549: 
550: ### Check for BSD or Apple libc library.
551: 
552: OCTAVE_BSD_LIBC
553: 
554: ### Check for pthread library.
555: 
556: AX_PTHREAD
557: dnl Include pthread libs and flags early in case other config tests need them.
558: dnl They seem to be required for the OpenGL tests on Debian systems.
559: LIBS="$PTHREAD_LIBS $LIBS"
560: XTRA_CFLAGS="$XTRA_CFLAGS $PTHREAD_CFLAGS"
561: XTRA_CXXFLAGS="$XTRA_CXXFLAGS $PTHREAD_CFLAGS"
562: dnl Set these for any other tests that may require them.
563: dnl They will be reset before output files are generated.
564: CFLAGS="$CFLAGS $PTHREAD_CFLAGS"
565: CXXFLAGS="$CXXFLAGS $PTHREAD_CFLAGS"
566: 
567: dnl Clang compiler will produce bogus warning during linking only.
568: AM_CONDITIONAL([AMCOND_CLANG_PTHREAD_WARNING],
569:                [test $ax_cv_PTHREAD_CLANG = yes])
570: 
571: dnl Check if glibc uses wrong stack size
572: OCTAVE_CHECK_BROKEN_PTHREAD_STACKSIZE
573: AM_CONDITIONAL([OCTAVE_CHECK_BROKEN_PTHREAD_STACKSIZE],
574:   [test $octave_cv_broken_pthread_stacksize = yes])
575: 
576: ### Test whether the compiler supports OpenMP.
577: dnl This is enabled by default to allow the option of using OpenMP in
578: dnl loadable modules.
579: 
580: ENABLE_OPENMP=no
581: check_for_openmp=yes
582: AC_ARG_ENABLE([openmp],
583:   [AS_HELP_STRING([--disable-openmp],
584:     [disable OpenMP SMP multi-threading])],
585:   [if test "$enableval" = no; then check_for_openmp=no; fi], [])
586: if test $check_for_openmp = yes; then
587:   AC_LANG_PUSH(C)
588:   AX_OPENMP([XTRA_CFLAGS="$XTRA_CFLAGS $OPENMP_CFLAGS"; ENABLE_OPENMP=yes], [])
589:   AC_LANG_POP(C)
590:   AC_LANG_PUSH(C++)
591:   AX_OPENMP([XTRA_CXXFLAGS="$XTRA_CXXFLAGS $OPENMP_CXXFLAGS"; ENABLE_OPENMP=yes], [])
592:   AC_LANG_POP(C++)
593: fi
594: 
595: dnl Set these for any other tests that may require them.
596: dnl They will be reset before output files are generated.
597: CFLAGS="$CFLAGS $OPENMP_CFLAGS"
598: CXXFLAGS="$CXXFLAGS $OPENMP_CXXFLAGS"

     yes | "")

### Determine C++ compiler capabilities.

if test $ENABLE_STD_PMR_POLYMORPHIC_ALLOCATOR = yes; then

else

fi

### Determine which C compiler to use (we expect to find gcc or clang).

AC_PROG_CC
AC_PROG_CPP

## Save and restore CFLAGS and CXXFLAGS globally.
dnl These variables are for users, so we shouldn't be touching them.
dnl Instead, we should set the corresponding AM_ flags (currently by way of the
dnl XTRA_ variables).  However, for the duration of the configure script, we
dnl may set CFLAGS and CXXFLAGS so that subsequent tests succeed.  Temporary
dnl settings like this are currently done for pthreads and openmp, for example.
original_octave_configure_CFLAGS="$CFLAGS"
original_octave_configure_CXXFLAGS="$CXXFLAGS"

## Check for MSVC
have_msvc=no
case $host_os in
  msdosmsvc)
    have_msvc=yes
  ;;
  mingw*)
    AC_MSG_CHECKING([for MSVC compiler])
    AC_PREPROC_IFELSE([AC_LANG_SOURCE([[
        #if ! defined (_MSC_VER)
        #error "Not MSVC compiler"
        #endif

      have_msvc=yes, have_msvc=no)
    AC_MSG_RESULT([$have_msvc])

esac

### gnulib initialization: part 1
dnl Must take place immediately after a compiler is determined

gl_EARLY

### Record version number when using g++.

    [octave_cv_gxx_version],
    [octave_cv_gxx_version=[`$CXX -v 2>&1 | $GREP "^.*g.. version" | $SED -e 's/^.*g.. version *//' -e 's/cygnus-//' -e 's/egcs-//' -e 's/ .*//'`]
  ])

fi

### Record version number when using gcc.
dnl It might be different from the g++ version number.

GCC_VERSION=

  AC_CACHE_CHECK([gcc compiler version number],
    [octave_cv_gcc_version],
    [octave_cv_gcc_version=[`$CC -v 2>&1 | $GREP "^.*gcc version" | $SED -e 's/^.*g.. version *//' -e 's/cygnus-//' -e 's/egcs-//' -e 's/ .*//'`]

## Assume GCC.

AC_CHECK_LIB(m, sin)

AC_CHECK_SIZEOF([int])

if test $ac_cv_sizeof_void_p -ge 8; then

else

fi

AC_ARG_ENABLE(64,
  [AS_HELP_STRING([--disable-64],
    [don't use 64-bit integers for array dimensions and indexing])],
  [case $enableval in
     yes) ENABLE_64=yes ;;
     no) ENABLE_64=no ;;

   esac])

if test $ENABLE_64 = yes; then
  if test $ac_cv_sizeof_void_p -ge 8; then
    OCTAVE_IDX_TYPE=int64_t
  else
    warn_64_bit="--enable-64 option given but pointers are less than 64-bits wide; disabling 64-bit indexing"
    OCTAVE_CONFIGURE_WARNING([warn_64_bit])
    OCTAVE_IDX_TYPE=int32_t
    ENABLE_64=no
  fi
else
  OCTAVE_IDX_TYPE=int32_t

AC_SUBST(ENABLE_64)
if test $ENABLE_64 = yes; then

  AC_DEFINE(OCTAVE_ENABLE_64, 1,
    [Define to 1 to use 64-bit integers for array dimensions and indexing.])
else
  octave_sizeof_octave_idx_type=4
fi

AC_DEFINE_UNQUOTED(OCTAVE_SIZEOF_IDX_TYPE, [$octave_sizeof_octave_idx_type],
  [Define to the size of the octave_idx_type (8 or 4).])

AC_SUBST(OCTAVE_IDX_TYPE)
AC_DEFINE_UNQUOTED(OCTAVE_IDX_TYPE, [$OCTAVE_IDX_TYPE],
  [Define to the type of octave_idx_type (64 or 32 bit signed integer).])

### Check for LLVM or Apple libc++ library.

OCTAVE_LLVM_LIBCXX

OCTAVE_BSD_LIBC

### Check for pthread library.

AX_PTHREAD
dnl Include pthread libs and flags early in case other config tests need them.
dnl They seem to be required for the OpenGL tests on Debian systems.
LIBS="$PTHREAD_LIBS $LIBS"
XTRA_CFLAGS="$XTRA_CFLAGS $PTHREAD_CFLAGS"
XTRA_CXXFLAGS="$XTRA_CXXFLAGS $PTHREAD_CFLAGS"
dnl Set these for any other tests that may require them.
dnl They will be reset before output files are generated.
CFLAGS="$CFLAGS $PTHREAD_CFLAGS"
CXXFLAGS="$CXXFLAGS $PTHREAD_CFLAGS"

dnl Clang compiler will produce bogus warning during linking only.
AM_CONDITIONAL([AMCOND_CLANG_PTHREAD_WARNING],
               [test $ax_cv_PTHREAD_CLANG = yes])

dnl Check if glibc uses wrong stack size
OCTAVE_CHECK_BROKEN_PTHREAD_STACKSIZE
AM_CONDITIONAL([OCTAVE_CHECK_BROKEN_PTHREAD_STACKSIZE],
  [test $octave_cv_broken_pthread_stacksize = yes])

### Test whether the compiler supports OpenMP.
dnl This is enabled by default to allow the option of using OpenMP in
dnl loadable modules.

ENABLE_OPENMP=no
check_for_openmp=yes
AC_ARG_ENABLE([openmp],
  [AS_HELP_STRING([--disable-openmp],
    [disable OpenMP SMP multi-threading])],
  [if test "$enableval" = no; then check_for_openmp=no; fi], [])
if test $check_for_openmp = yes; then
  AC_LANG_PUSH(C)
  AX_OPENMP([XTRA_CFLAGS="$XTRA_CFLAGS $OPENMP_CFLAGS"; ENABLE_OPENMP=yes], [])
  AC_LANG_POP(C)
  AC_LANG_PUSH(C++)
  AX_OPENMP([XTRA_CXXFLAGS="$XTRA_CXXFLAGS $OPENMP_CXXFLAGS"; ENABLE_OPENMP=yes], [])
  AC_LANG_POP(C++)
fi

dnl Set these for any other tests that may require them.
dnl They will be reset before output files are generated.
CFLAGS="$CFLAGS $OPENMP_CFLAGS"
CXXFLAGS="$CXXFLAGS $OPENMP_CXXFLAGS"

### Check for either of GraphicsMagick++/ImageMagick++ libraries.

check_magick=yes
use_magick=no
AC_ARG_WITH([magick],
  [AS_HELP_STRING([--with-magick=LIB],
    [select library to use for image I/O (options: GraphicsMagick++ (default) or ImageMagick++)])
dnl Second help string must not be indented for correct alignment
AS_HELP_STRING([--without-magick], [don't use Magick library, disable imread, imwrite, imformats, imfinfo])],
  [case $withval in
     yes | "")
       magick="GraphicsMagick++"
     ;;
     no)
       check_magick=no
     ;;
     *)
       magick="$withval"
     ;;
   esac],
  [magick="GraphicsMagick++"])

if test $check_magick = yes; then

  MAGICK_CPPFLAGS=
  MAGICK_LDFLAGS=
  MAGICK_LIBS=

  PKG_CHECK_EXISTS([$magick], [
    dnl We are using --cflags now instead of --cflags-only-I because some
    dnl Graphics/ImageMagick++ packages will provide -D options for
    dnl MAGICKCORE_HDRI_ENABLE and MAGICKCORE_QUANTUM_DEPTH that are needed
    dnl for building with a particular verison of the library.  If there
    dnl are other flags in the output from pkg-config --cflags that cause
    dnl trouble, then we may need to go back to using --cflags-only-I and
    dnl have a configure test to determine the proper definitions of
    dnl MAGICKCORE_HDRI_ENABLE and MAGICKCORE_QUANTUM_DEPTH.
    dnl See also bug #49563.
    MAGICK_CPPFLAGS="$($PKG_CONFIG --cflags $magick | $SED -e 's/^ *$//')"
    MAGICK_LDFLAGS="$($PKG_CONFIG --libs-only-L $magick | $SED -e 's/^ *$//')"
    MAGICK_LIBS="$($PKG_CONFIG --libs-only-l $magick | $SED -e 's/^ *$//')"

    warn_magick="$magick library fails tests.  The imread, imwrite, and imfinfo functions for reading and writing image files will not be fully functional."

    save_CPPFLAGS="$CPPFLAGS"
    save_LIBS="$LIBS"
    CPPFLAGS="$MAGICK_CPPFLAGS $CPPFLAGS"
    LIBS="$MAGICK_LDFLAGS $MAGICK_LIBS $LIBS"
    AC_LANG_PUSH(C++)
    AC_CHECK_HEADER([Magick++.h], [
      AC_CACHE_CHECK([for Magick::ColorRGB and Magick::PixelPacket in Magick++.h],
        [octave_cv_func_magick],
        [AC_LINK_IFELSE([AC_LANG_PROGRAM([[
          #include <Magick++.h>
          ]], [[
          Magick::ColorRGB c;
          Magick::PixelPacket pix;
          ]])],
          octave_cv_func_magick=yes,
          octave_cv_func_magick=no)
        ])
      if test $octave_cv_func_magick = yes; then
        use_magick=yes
        warn_magick=
      fi
    ])
    AC_LANG_POP(C++)
    CPPFLAGS="$save_CPPFLAGS"
    LIBS="$save_LIBS"
  ],
  [use_magick=no
   warn_magick="$magick library not found.  The imread, imwrite, and imfinfo functions for reading and writing image files will not be fully functional."])
fi

if test $use_magick = yes; then

    ## Only include -I options in FLTK_CPPFLAGS
    fltk_cflags=`$FLTK_CONFIG $fltkconf_args --use-gl --cflags`
    for fltk_option in $fltk_cflags; do
      case $fltk_option in

        ;;
      esac
    done
    FLTK_CPPFLAGS=`echo "$FLTK_CPPFLAGS" | $SED -e 's/^ \+//'`

    ## Split -L and -l options into FLTK_LDFLAGS and FLTK_LIBS
    fltk_ldflags=`$FLTK_CONFIG $fltkconf_args --use-gl --ldflags`
    for fltk_option in $fltk_ldflags; do
      case $fltk_option in

        ;;
        *)

        ;;

    done
    FLTK_LIBS=`echo "$FLTK_LIBS" | $SED -e 's/^ \+//'`

AC_SUBST(JAR)
AC_SUBST(JAR_SUPPORTS_DATE)
AC_SUBST(JAVA_CPPFLAGS)
AC_SUBST(JAVA_LIBS)
AC_DEFINE_UNQUOTED([JAVA_HOME], ["$JAVA_HOME"], [Java home (top-level installation dir)])
AC_DEFINE_UNQUOTED([JAVA_LDPATH], ["$JAVA_LDPATH"], [Java library path (libjvm)])

### Determine if documentation should and can be built.

ENABLE_DOCS=yes
AC_ARG_ENABLE([docs],
  [AS_HELP_STRING([--disable-docs], [don't build documentation files])],
  [if test "$enableval" = no; then
     ENABLE_DOCS=no
     warn_docs="building documentation disabled; make dist will fail."
     OCTAVE_CONFIGURE_WARNING([warn_docs])
   fi], [])

if test $ENABLE_DOCS = yes; then
  if test $opengl_graphics = no; then
    if test -n "$warn_gnuplot"; then
      ENABLE_DOCS=no
      warn_docs_graphics="building documentation disabled because no suitable graphics toolkit is available; make dist will fail."
      OCTAVE_CONFIGURE_WARNING([warn_docs_graphics])
    fi
  fi
  if test -n "$warn_makeinfo"; then
    ENABLE_DOCS=no
    warn_docs_makeinfo="building documentation disabled because makeinfo was not found or does not support @sortas; make dist will fail."
    OCTAVE_CONFIGURE_WARNING([warn_docs_makeinfo])
  fi
fi
if test $ENABLE_DOCS = yes; then
  AC_DEFINE(ENABLE_DOCS, 1,
    [Define to 1 to build Octave documentation files.])
fi

AM_CONDITIONAL([AMCOND_BUILD_DOCS], [test $ENABLE_DOCS = yes])

AM_CONDITIONAL([AMCOND_BUILD_QT_DOCS],
               [test $ENABLE_DOCS = yes && test $build_qt_gui = yes])

OCTAVE_RELOCATE_ALL=no
AC_ARG_ENABLE([relocate-all],
  [AS_HELP_STRING([--enable-relocate-all],
    [assume that all dependencies that are installed under the same prefix are relocated when Octave is relocated])],
  [if test "$enableval" = yes; then OCTAVE_RELOCATE_ALL=yes; fi], [])
AC_SUBST(OCTAVE_RELOCATE_ALL)
if test $OCTAVE_RELOCATE_ALL = yes; then
  AC_DEFINE(OCTAVE_REPLACE_PREFIX, 1, [Replace prefix in mkoctfile flags.])
fi
AM_CONDITIONAL([AMCOND_RELOCATE_ALL], [test $OCTAVE_RELOCATE_ALL = yes])

OCTAVE_RELOCATE_WITH_CYGPATH="no"
CYGPATH=""
if test $OCTAVE_RELOCATE_ALL = yes; then
  case $host_os in
    mingw*)
      # If this is on MSYS2, paths (including the installation prefix) can be
      # represented in UNIX or Windows compatible form.  The prefix should be
      # relocated no matter in which form it appears.

      # Check for the tool "cygpath" that can be used to convert between the
      # different forms.
      AC_CHECK_TOOL(CYGPATH, [cygpath])
      if test -n "$CYGPATH"; then
        OCTAVE_RELOCATE_WITH_CYGPATH="yes"
      fi
    ;;
  esac
fi
AC_SUBST(OCTAVE_RELOCATE_WITH_CYGPATH)
AC_SUBST(CYGPATH)

ENABLE_HG_ID=yes

  [if test "$enableval" = no; then ENABLE_HG_ID=no; fi], [])
AM_CONDITIONAL([AMCOND_ENABLE_HG_ID], [test $ENABLE_HG_ID = yes])

### Determine whether to install build logs with Octave.

install_build_logs=no
AC_ARG_ENABLE([install-build-logs],
  [AS_HELP_STRING([--enable-install-build-logs],
    [install build logs (i.e., config.log) with Octave])],
  [if test "$enableval" = yes; then install_build_logs=yes; fi])
AM_CONDITIONAL([AMCOND_INSTALL_BUILD_LOGS], [test $install_build_logs = yes])

  [AS_HELP_STRING([--disable-lib-visibility-flags],
    [don't build libraries with visibility flags (export all symbols)])],
  [case $enableval in
     yes) ENABLE_LIB_VISIBILITY_FLAGS=yes ;;
     no) ENABLE_LIB_VISIBILITY_FLAGS=no ;;
     *) AC_MSG_ERROR([bad value $enableval for --enable-lib-visibility-flags]) ;;
   esac])

case $host_os in
  msdosmsvc | mingw* | cygwin*)
    # Assume that symbol export is working on that platform
  ;;
  *)
    if test $ENABLE_LIB_VISIBILITY_FLAGS = yes && test $HAVE_VISIBILITY = 0; then
      AC_MSG_NOTICE([cannot build with visibility flags on this platform])
      ENABLE_LIB_VISIBILITY_FLAGS=no
    fi
  ;;
esac

if test $ENABLE_LIB_VISIBILITY_FLAGS = yes; then
  AC_DEFINE(OCTAVE_ENABLE_LIB_VISIBILITY_FLAGS, 1,
    [Define to 1 if building libraries with visibility flags])
else
  case $host_os in
    msdosmsvc | mingw* | cygwin*)
      LDFLAGS="$LDFLAGS -Wl,--export-all-symbols"
    ;;
  esac
fi

AM_CONDITIONAL([AMCOND_LIB_VISIBILITY_FLAGS],
  [test $ENABLE_LIB_VISIBILITY_FLAGS = yes])
